title: 542. Generate Random Point in a Circle

examples.explanation: Any point within distance 1 of the origin is accepted; returning the center itself is valid.
The center (3,-1) is distance 0 from itself, so it is always a valid (though not uniform) answer.
Both the center and any point within 5.0 of (2,-3) pass the checker.

hints: Sample uniformly by area: scale the radius by sqrt(u) for u uniform in [0,1), with the angle uniform in [0, 2*pi).
Convert the polar offset back with cosine and sine, then shift by (xCenter, yCenter).
The judge checks only that each point lies within the circle (with a tiny tolerance), not the distribution.
